summary: Core FsQuint depends on FSharp.Core, not FS-GG SDD/Coordination runtime packages; Tooling references core and provisions nothing. The process request carries executable SHA256/version, working directory, source/module, timeout/output cap and selected command; Tooling checks identity, interprets positive scenario evidence and retires owned processes on cancellation/output limits. The release workflow qualifies/packs the coherent core+Tooling source and pushes identical archives to both feeds, then performs readback and anonymous consumer checks. README install0.1.0 and compatibility FSharp.Core floor10.1.302 describe accepted release support, while current source.props selects0.1.1/Core10.1.401: do not silently transfer archive or consumer evidence between these tuples. Tool pins are separate from package updates, and no automatic runtime adoption follows from a source or dependency merge.
title: Package, executable and provider pins carry distinct claims
